buttonLabel: "Explore the culture of Brazil, Colombia and Ecuador"
lead: >-
  A cultural route through Brazil, Ecuador and Colombia brings together Rio de Janeiro's urban scenery, Quito's colonial center and several eras of Colombian history, from fortified Cartagena to Bogotá's museums. On Ada Tours' current itinerary these stops are part of a journey through eight countries. Choose it by comparing the allocation of sightseeing days, museums and transfer times.
---

## Three countries and three perspectives on urban history

**Brazil, Ecuador and Colombia offer completely different cultural experiences on one long itinerary.** In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), travelers visit Corcovado and Christ the Redeemer, Sugarloaf Mountain and the city center. Here Rio is experienced through its architecture, bay and surrounding mountains. The city's combined natural and urban landscape, including the area of [Tijuca National Park](/brazil/place/tijuca-national-park/), is recognized by UNESCO as a cultural landscape shaped by the relationship between city, mountains and sea.

The Ecuadorian stage focuses mainly on [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/). The itinerary includes the historic center, church architecture and the equator line. UNESCO highlights Quito's preserved colonial city plan and its local Baroque school, in which European artistic traditions merged with the work of local craftspeople. This is visible in church facades, interiors and the layout of old neighborhoods. After Quito the tour heads to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/), whose main value on this itinerary is natural, so presenting a sea day as another historical excursion would be misleading.

In Colombia, cultural history continues through several stops. Medellín features a city tour including [Comuna 13](/colombia/place/comuna-13/). [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) then reveals another era: a Spanish colonial port with fortifications and historic Caribbean neighborhoods. [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) includes the Gold Museum, the Botero Collection, La Candelaria historic center and Monserrate. An additional day is devoted to the underground Salt Cathedral in Zipaquirá.

## Which excursions actually have time allocated

On the [32-day itinerary through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), the Brazilian stage runs from arrival in São Paulo to Iguazú Falls. Rio's principal city excursions occupy two separate days. Ecuador follows the Andean route through Chile, Bolivia and Peru, with a sightseeing day in Quito and several island days before departure via Guayaquil. Colombia ends the journey: Medellín, Guatapé, Cartagena, Bogotá and Zipaquirá.

Thus this catalog title defines **an intersection of countries and a cultural interest**, not a separate short three-country itinerary. Travelers pass through Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Peru between Brazil and Ecuador. A shorter journey would need a separately designed itinerary and connections.

The selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. Compare the complete geography in the [Brazil, Colombia and Ecuador catalog](/multi-country/brazil_colombia_ecuador/), or explore more destinations in [multi-country culture and history tours](/multi-country/interests/culture-and-history/).

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

## Which cultural experiences differ most?

| Stop | What it reveals |
|---|---|
| Rio | Landscape, 20th-century architecture and the bay |
| Quito | Colonial Baroque and the urban center |
| Cartagena | Maritime port and fortifications |
| Bogotá | Pre-Hispanic collections and art |

Brazilian culture on this itinerary is closely tied to urban space: Rio's viewpoints show how buildings fit between the shore and steep slopes. For a more focused Brazil journey, see [culture and history tours](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/brazil/).

Ecuador deserves consideration as more than a connection to the Galápagos. A full day in Quito offers an introduction to the historic center, after which the journey moves to the islands' protected natural environment. [Culture and history tours in Ecuador](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/ecuador/) let you compare itineraries with different time allocations.

Colombia offers a longer sequence of urban experiences. [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) adds local architecture and painted facades; Cartagena offers colonial defenses; and Bogotá has museum collections and city life. [Colombian history and culture tours](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/colombia/) provide an opportunity to focus on the country without crossing the whole continent.

## What to consider when choosing dates and excursions

Check the actual days of the week for museums. The Bogotá itinerary specifically states that the Gold Museum closes on Mondays, while the Mint and Botero Collection close on Tuesdays. If the order of flights changes, museum visits must be rearranged. Quito's sightseeing takes place at over 2,800 meters above sea level, so walking time and acclimatization deserve attention after a flight.

The difference between Cartagena's coastal heat and Quito's cool high-altitude evenings affects packing more than a simple country list might suggest. We help coordinate city excursions, flights and rest intervals while retaining the selected key sights. Entry rules for each nationality and current visitor conditions are checked when preparing the trip.

## Frequently asked questions about cultural travel through Brazil, Ecuador and Colombia

### Can I choose just these three countries without the other five?

Yes, as a tailor-made itinerary. The existing connected program visits eight countries, so a standalone three-country trip requires different flights, duration and excursion arrangements.

### Which city has the most museums on this itinerary?

In Colombia, Bogotá has the richest museum day, including the Gold Museum, Botero Collection and historic center. Quito and Cartagena focus more on architecture and walks through historic neighborhoods.

### Must I visit the Galápagos for Ecuadorian history?

No. On the existing tour, the Galápagos are included for nature and a boat excursion. A custom program could combine Quito with another Ecuadorian region if history and culture are the priority.

### Can I explore Cartagena's entire historic center in one day?

The 32-day itinerary includes a sightseeing tour of Cartagena's principal sights. More detailed visits to museums and individual neighborhoods require extra time, to be agreed when changing the itinerary.

lead: >-
  Brazilian Iguazú, the island nature of the Galápagos and the reservoir near Guatapé in Colombia can be experienced on one long journey. The nature stops are different, however: the Galápagos feature island outings, while Colombia offers panoramic scenery rather than a dedicated safari.
---

## Brazil, Ecuador and Colombia: where nature features on the route

In the [Brazil–Colombia–Ecuador combination](/multi-country/brazil_colombia_ecuador/), the nature theme is based on actual stops rather than a promise of identical excursions in each country. Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. It is a [32-day journey through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/); in addition to these three it visits Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Peru.

For nature lovers, the itinerary offers three experiences: the Iguazú Falls system, the protected natural areas of the Galápagos and green hills around the Guatapé reservoir. City tours and multi-day transfers separate them. This is a broad introduction to South America, not a specialist expedition to three national parks.

## Iguazú in Brazil: panoramic sightseeing, not a jungle safari

After Rio de Janeiro the group reaches [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The Brazilian side of the waterfalls is visited on an included excursion with a Russian-speaking guide. The Argentine side is visited the following day before the itinerary continues to Buenos Aires.

Here the principal natural attraction is water cascading over rock ledges amid humid forest and viewpoint paths. The Bird Park and Macuco Safari are listed as optional paid activities. Therefore, anyone choosing the trip specifically for wildlife should also examine the [“Wildlife and Safaris” interest](/interests/wildlife/) and exactly which excursions are included.

Brazil's stage invites comparison with the islands of Ecuador: at Iguazú, visitors mainly observe nature from prepared trails and platforms; in the Galápagos, a day is organized around a specific island excursion.

## Ecuador: Santa Cruz and one alternative island outing

The [32-day journey](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) reaches Ecuador after the Andean stages through Chile, Bolivia and Peru. It includes Quito and a flight to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/), where travelers explore Santa Cruz and its highland areas.

One of the following days features **North Seymour and Bachas Beach, or South Plaza and Cape Carrión**. These are alternatives, not four visits in one day. To know which landscapes and wildlife encounters are actually possible, confirm the assigned island route and current national park rules for your dates.

Ecuador's nature stage differs from Quito's city sightseeing. The country appearing on an itinerary does not mean every day there is devoted to wildlife. For other choices, explore [Ecuador nature tours](/interests/nature/tours/ecuador/).

## Colombia: Guatapé's landscapes after the islands

The itinerary then leads from Guayaquil to Medellín. The Colombian stage includes a visit to El Peñón rock and [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/), with views over a large reservoir. Travelers see mountainous relief, small islands and green shores while also exploring the town itself.

Other Colombian stops — Medellín, Cartagena, [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) and Zipaquirá — offer numerous cultural and urban experiences. The published program **does not advertise a standalone Colombian safari or an Amazon excursion**. It would be inaccurate to describe the entire Colombian stage as travel through wild forest.

If landscape photography is your main wish, this Colombian stop may complement the Galápagos. If you want several days watching animals in nature reserves, you need another itinerary: [Colombia nature tours](/interests/nature/tours/colombia/) can be compared by their actual places and activities.

## What these three countries offer — and what they do not

| Country | Actual nature highlight |
|---|---|
| Brazil | Iguazú cascades |
| Ecuador | Santa Cruz island and highlands |
| Colombia | Guatapé rock and reservoir |

Together, travelers encounter waterfalls, protected islands and a mountain reservoir. Yet these involve different formats: a sightseeing trail, an island trip following an agreed alternative and a panoramic road excursion. Compare the duration of each stop against the full daily itinerary.

The three countries are also **not consecutive** on the published tour: other countries lie between the Brazilian and Ecuadorian nature stages. Shortening the route changes flights, duration and logistics. Ada Tours helps coordinate the selected sequence, overnight stays and site access, with transit and immigration requirements checked for every actual border and traveler nationality, not merely these three countries.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Brazil, Colombia and Ecuador

### Is a full safari in Colombia included?

No. The Colombian section of the published [long tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) includes Guatapé and city excursions, but no separate safari.

### Are all the Galápagos Islands visited?

No. The itinerary includes Santa Cruz and one of two alternative island outings. The archipelago's complete island list cannot be treated as included.

### Is a standalone journey through just these three countries available?

This selection features three countries within a longer tour. A separate route would need individually calculated flights and days; [all multi-country nature journeys](/multi-country/interests/nature/) offer options for comparison.

### Should I choose Guatapé or spend more days in the Galápagos?

Guatapé provides mountain scenery and reservoir views, while the Galápagos offer island nature and regulated national-park excursions. The choice depends on whether you want a broad variety of landscapes or a deeper exploration of one archipelago.

## Where to watch wild animals on the route through Brazil, Colombia and Ecuador

**The richest wildlife-watching program within this combination is in Ecuador's Galápagos Islands.** In the [Santa Cruz highlands](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-highlands/), an [excursion to giant tortoises and lava tunnels](/ecuador/santa-cruz-highlands/santa-cruz-highlands-lava-tunnels/) is scheduled. Travelers can watch tortoises in their natural habitat and learn about the volcanic landscape and conservation system. Sightings depend on wild animals' behavior, so no particular number can be guaranteed.

The next day in the [Galápagos](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) includes **one of two boat routes**. The first covers North Seymour and Bachas Beach, with seabirds such as frigatebirds and blue-footed boobies and coastal ecosystems. The second visits South Plaza and Cape Carrión, offering a different set of island nature experiences. The choice is made when confirming the program; promising both on a single day would be incorrect. Protected-area regulations, permitted routes and authorized guides apply throughout the archipelago.

Brazil offers a different kind of nature experience. In [Tijuca National Park](/brazil/place/tijuca-national-park/), travelers encounter forested slopes around [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). The journey then reaches [Iguazú Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), where the main excursion introduces the river, cascades and tropical vegetation. **The Bird Park at Iguazú is an optional excursion**, not an included visit. The standard tour does not guarantee encounters with particular animal species in Brazil.

Colombia is represented by Medellín, [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/), Cartagena and Bogotá. Green hills and the reservoir near Guatapé offer beautiful nature views, but **no dedicated birdwatching or wildlife expedition is listed on the Colombian stage**. The “Wildlife and Safaris” label applies to the whole journey because of its Galápagos excursions, not automatically to each country and day.

## What the existing multi-country program includes

The [32-day tour through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) follows Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador and Colombia in that order. Brazilian nature excursions occur early in the journey, while the Galápagos come close to the end, after a long Andean stage and several international flights. This page highlights three principal countries under the wildlife theme; it does not mean a separate journey limited to them.

This intersection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. View the full countries and related trips in the [Brazil, Colombia and Ecuador catalog](/multi-country/brazil_colombia_ecuador/). For other destinations, explore the [multi-country wildlife-watching selection](/multi-country/interests/wildlife/).

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

## Choosing a route for your main wildlife goal

| Goal | What to focus on |
|---|---|
| Volcanic islands | Galápagos, Santa Cruz |
| Seabirds | The confirmed island boat trip |
| Waterfalls and forest | Iguazú, Tijuca |
| Mountain panoramas | Guatapé |

For travelers whose main goal is tortoises and birds, start with [wildlife-watching tours in Ecuador](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/), compare island days and alternative boat routes. For humid forest and waterfalls, examine [Brazil nature journeys](/interests/nature/tours/brazil/). [Colombia nature tours](/interests/nature/tours/colombia/) should be compared by the landscapes and places actually visited. When wildlife is the priority, check the relevant observation days: the mere presence of a country on a multi-country itinerary does not confirm them.

On the Galápagos, visitor discipline matters: remain on marked trails, keep your distance from animals, do not feed them and follow the guide's instructions. For a boat excursion, bring sun and wind protection, suitable landing footwear and waterproof protection for belongings. Equipment and swimming arrangements depend on the confirmed island-day option.

## Logistics for nature lovers

The principal challenge of this combination is the considerable distance between nature stops. From Rio, the journey heads to Iguazú and then across other countries and high-altitude regions to Quito. The Galápagos require a separate flight and crossing to Santa Cruz. After the islands, travelers fly via Guayaquil to Colombia. Travel time cannot all be counted as wildlife-watching days.

If you want more time with animals, it makes more sense to discuss allocating additional days to the Galápagos than simply adding another country. We can coordinate the route and confirmed sites according to available island excursions and flight times. Current conservation restrictions and access rules must also be checked before travel, as permitted areas may change.

## Frequently asked questions about nature journeys through Brazil, Ecuador and Colombia

### Where are most wildlife encounters scheduled on this tour?

In the Galápagos: Santa Cruz's highlands have an excursion to giant tortoises, followed by one of two island boat routes. Observations take place in natural habitats, with no guarantee of any particular animal.

### Is the Iguazú Bird Park included in the price?

No. On the current 32-day program, the Bird Park is optional. The principal nature excursion in Brazil focuses on the Brazilian side of the waterfalls.

### Is there a separate safari or birdwatching activity in Colombia?

No such activities are listed for this tour. Colombia's stage focuses on cities, Guatapé and cultural sightseeing. To watch wildlife in Colombia, choose a different route with the relevant days.

### Can I take both Galápagos boat-day options?

The existing tour includes one of two options: North Seymour and Bachas, or South Plaza and Cape Carrión. Both are not promised together; the choice is confirmed when booking.

## Brazil, Peru, Ecuador and Colombia: cities, archaeology and nature

**Each country has its own role in this combination.** Brazil brings Rio and Iguazú Falls; Peru offers Inca history; Ecuador the Galápagos Islands; and Colombia cities in the Andes and on the Caribbean coast. The current selection includes the four countries **as part of** a [32-day program through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Between Brazil and Peru, the route visits Argentina, Uruguay, Chile and Bolivia.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. Find the exact price, duration and complete country list in the existing tour description.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

| Country | Main reason to visit |
|---|---|
| Brazil | Rio and the waterfalls |
| Peru | Cusco and Machu Picchu |
| Ecuador | Galápagos and Quito |
| Colombia | Medellín, Cartagena, Bogotá |

Anyone wanting just these four countries without the others needs a separate tailored program. The existing tour cannot be described as a four-country journey merely because the site lets you select them as filters.

## Brazil: what is actually included before Peru

After arriving in São Paulo, travelers fly to [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). Sightseeing covers Corcovado, Christ the Redeemer, Sugarloaf Mountain and the old city. The group then flies to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) to explore the Brazilian side of the waterfalls.

The following day visits the Argentine side of Iguazú and ends with a flight to Buenos Aires. This is **a separate international border crossing** and must be included in document checks. The Bird Park and Macuco Safari are optional paid excursions, not mandatory parts of the included sightseeing day.

Brazil's stage involves several flights and busy city sightseeing. It is not a week-long beach holiday, even though Rio stands beside the ocean. For longer coastal relaxation, compare [Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/) and their daily itineraries.

## Peru: Machu Picchu after high-altitude Bolivia

The route enters [Peru](/peru/) overland from Bolivia via Desaguadero. Travelers visit [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), then take a tourist bus to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), from where they visit [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). Historic Cusco sights and a flight to [Lima](/peru/place/lima/) follow.

The transport sequence matters: a bus day between Puno and Cusco, a train and excursion to Machu Picchu, and a flight to Lima. All this takes time. The Puno day cannot be casually removed or rest after the highlands shortened while assuming every confirmed subsequent ticket will still work.

Before Peru, the Bolivian stage crosses high-altitude lagoons and Uyuni. So it is important to consider **all preceding altitude exposure**, even though Bolivia is not named in this selection. Travelers with cardiovascular or respiratory conditions may benefit from personalized medical advice and insurance appropriate to the actual route.

## Ecuador: Quito and the Galápagos are two distinct experiences

A flight from Lima takes the group to [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/), followed by city sightseeing and a trip to the equator. The next flight reaches the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/): Santa Cruz Island, its highlands, Puerto Ayora and a boat excursion.

The sea day offers alternatives. **One of two options is included**: North Seymour and Bachas, or South Plaza and Cape Carrión. The choice depends on confirmation after booking. It would be a mistake to promise both routes or a full multi-day cruise: the existing tour is based on Santa Cruz with a separate boat trip.

Before visiting the archipelago, check the TCT card, conservation fees, food import rules and protection requirements for island ecosystems. Fees depend on visitor category. Confirm separately whether they are included in the package. If animals are your main interest, compare [Ecuador wildlife tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/) with longer observation programs.

## Colombia: three different city experiences

After the Galápagos, the group returns to Guayaquil and flies to [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). A trip to Guatapé and Comuna 13 follows, then a flight to [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) and a separate city sightseeing day. The final stage is [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), including Monserrate and a visit to [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/).

Colombia offers several contrasting experiences: Medellín's mountain-city landscape, Cartagena's historic center and Bogotá's museums. Although Cartagena is on the Caribbean coast, the itinerary does not provide a separate multi-day beach holiday. It cannot be added to the description without a separate itinerary change.

There are domestic flights between Colombian regions. Any change to the number of days must start with checking their schedules and city order, then coordinating sightseeing and accommodation.

## Documents, tickets and money for four countries

For the existing tour, check entry rules **for all eight countries**, including Argentina and Bolivia, even if only four are your primary interest. Visa, passport validity, additional documentation and health regulations differ by nationality. On this itinerary Ecuador is reached by air from Lima, which differs from crossing its land border.

Brazilian reais, Peruvian soles, US dollars in Ecuador and Colombian pesos require separate planning for exchange and payment. Do not assume that any bank card works equally across the four countries. We help coordinate the order of flights and transfers, review documentation and compare payment options by stage.

The full package includes 4-star hotels, domestic flights, tickets and scheduled excursions. International flights and optional activities listed separately are not included. Shortening the tour to four countries requires a new price and inclusions calculation.

## How to tell if this journey suits you

Its strength is the rapid change of experiences: a city and tropical waterfalls, Andean archaeology, island nature and Colombian historic neighborhoods. The trade-off is numerous flights and limited time at each stop. If exploring one country in greater depth matters more, compare [Peru tours](/peru/tour/), [Ecuador tours](/ecuador/tour/) and [Colombia journeys](/colombia/tour/). All available combinations appear in the [multi-country travel catalog](/multi-country/).

## Frequently asked questions about Brazil, Peru, Ecuador and Colombia

### Are all four countries consecutive on the route?

No. Brazil comes at the start of the 32-day journey. Argentina, Uruguay, Chile and Bolivia lie between Brazil and Peru; Peru, Ecuador and Colombia then follow in sequence.

### Can I visit just Machu Picchu and the Galápagos?

That shorter format would need a separate program with new flights, excursion tickets and price calculations. The existing 32-day tour is not an already approved shorter version.

### Is there a multi-day Galápagos cruise?

No. The itinerary uses Santa Cruz as a base with one of two alternative boat excursions.

### Are there beach days in Colombia?

The program features Cartagena and city sightseeing there. No special extended beach stay is included in the current schedule.

## Which adventures are actually included on this four-country route?

Our selection includes the [“Eight South American Countries in 32 Days” journey](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). These four countries **are part of its geography**, not a separate short tour. Stages in Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Peru also lie between Brazil, Ecuador and Colombia. Visiting just four countries would require a change to the entire program.

The main adventure feature is **the alternation of different kinds of activity**. Some days involve walking around natural attractions; others include boat excursions, viewpoints or drives along high-altitude roads. The catalog includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

We **do not promise multi-day trekking on the Inca Trail, an ascent of El Peñón or scuba diving**. If one of these is the primary objective, a different itinerary should be selected rather than treating it as part of this overview tour.

## Brazil: Iguazú Falls and an optional boat trip

Brazil begins with [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) and visits to Corcovado and Sugarloaf Mountain. Transport and city sightseeing take travelers to the viewpoints, so these days cannot be treated as mountaineering or challenging hiking. They provide a good introduction to Rio's topography and panoramas.

The route then reaches [Iguazú](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), with an included group excursion to the Brazilian side of the waterfalls and a Russian-speaking guide. Walkways and the proximity of powerful cascades are impressive without additional activities. Humidity, spray and possibly wet surfaces make footwear with a reliable grip important.

An extra option is **Macuco Safari**, combining a forest journey and a motorboat trip towards the falls. On the eight-country tour it **is optional and costs extra**. Not everyone automatically goes on the boat; contents, potential restrictions and price should be agreed in advance. [Iguazú Bird Park](/brazil/place/parque-das-aves/) is also a separate paid option, focusing on birds.

## Colombia: Guatapé and panoramas without invented extreme sports

Colombia begins in [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). The [El Peñol and Guatapé excursion](/colombia/medellin/el-penol-guatape-from-medellin/) visits El Peñón rock, the reservoir and [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) with its brightly painted facades. The appeal lies in the distinctive mountain landscape, viewpoints and Colombian towns.

**An organized ascent of the rock, technical climbing, rafting or a long trek are not specified as included in the confirmed excursion.** These cannot automatically be added to the tour description. Travelers wishing to climb the steps to El Peñón's summit must separately check current access rules and time available. A visit to the rock does not prove that admission or an ascent is included.

The following day explores [Medellín and Comuna 13](/colombia/medellin/medellin-city-and-comuna-13/), before a flight to [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/). The route then continues to [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) and the Salt Cathedral in Zipaquirá. This is a busy cultural and city stage that needs no invented sporting activities to justify the “adventure” label.

## Ecuador: island trails, boats and two distinct alternatives

From [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/) the group flies to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). On [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/), the itinerary visits the [highlands and lava tunnels](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-highlands/), followed by a stay in Puerto Ayora.

The following day features **one of two included alternatives**:

- [North Seymour](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) and Bachas Beach: boat travel, landing and observation of seabirds and the island coast.
- [South Plaza](/ecuador/place/south-plaza-island/) and Cape Carrión: an island trail and a marine stop on a separate route.

**Both islands are not visited on the same day.** The route is confirmed after booking; sea conditions and landing feasibility depend on the weather and protected-area rules. Snorkeling is mentioned in the island alternatives, but specific conditions and equipment need checking; **scuba diving is not advertised**.

Adventure here chiefly involves nature observation and a sea crossing. ## Frequently asked questions about adventure in four countries

### Is trekking along the Inca Trail included?

No. On this itinerary, Machu Picchu is visited on an excursion from Cusco with train travel.

### Is Macuco Safari at Iguazú included?

It is an optional paid excursion, not an obligatory part of the included waterfall visit.

### Can I visit both North Seymour and South Plaza?

One of the two routes is selected for the boat day. Visiting both would require a different program.

### Is climbing El Peñón in Colombia included?

The confirmed excursion includes the rock and Guatapé area, but does not guarantee reaching the summit.

### Where are the highest elevations on the trip?

The full journey's most significant high-altitude transfers pass through Bolivia, with additional highland stops in Peru. Bolivia is not named among the four selected countries but is part of the actual tour.
